newsitem.title: USA: Miami police nab "doctor" after botched implant.
newsitem.headline: Miami police nab "doctor" after botched implant.

text.p: An unlicensed doctor who left a woman in severe pain after a breast implant was arrested by Miami police after offering to perform liposuction on an undercover investigator, police said on Thursday.

Henry Castillo, 37, allegedly botched the breast implant operation on Brandi Saa so badly that infection set in. "She went to another doctor and then came forward to us," police Lt. Robert Lynch told Reuters.

Castillo was arrested on Wednesday after detectives taped a meeting at which he offered to perform surgery on a woman who was actually an investigator. "He told us he was a doctor, he offered us a price for surgery, we arrested him," Lynch said. "He is not licensed to practice in Florida."
The operating room was "not very sterile. There was dried blood on the floor," he added.

Castillo had agreed to operate on Saa if she would work for him part time. On the day of her breast enlargement operation no anaesthetist was available so local anaesthetic was used. When she complained of fever and pain she was allegedly told to use ice.
"She has been through a great ordeal. Thanks to the police no one else will fall victim to this man," said Saa's lawyer, Bruce Lehr.
Castillo told police he had credentials from Nicaragua, his home country. His cards listed specialities including plastic surgery, laser surgery and gynecology.
He has performed surgery on many people at the Inter-American Medical and Surgical Centre in North Miami. More than 25 other patients had now come to police with complaints, Lynch said.
Castillo has been charged with two counts of practicing medicine without a license and one count of trafficking in drugs, relating to issuing prescriptions.
